subject: On-prem telemetry conduit and SIEM onboarding for Aurelia Systems
messages:
From: Jessica Lang <jessica.lang@aurelia-sys.com>

Cc: Aurelia Security <security@aurelia-sys.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Observability onboarding for on-prem Redwood instance

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Aurelia is moving forward with a private Redwood deployment inside our datacenter and we need to lock down the observability handoff so our SOC and SIEM ingest meet audit requirements.

Quick context: we run Splunk Enterprise for log storage (HEC + heavy forwarder for older clusters) and use a centralized tracing backend (Tempo). Our security team needs a short runbook describing:
- what telemetry Redwood will export (syslog vs HEC vs S3 export)
- network ports, expected outbound flows, and cert trust model
- evidence artifacts for SOC 2 (delivery logs, signing, export hashes)

I attached a short requirements doc to start (aurelia-siem-requirements.pdf). Can your team confirm the recommended on-prem connector pattern and a staging acceptance checklist? Also, we may need a brief in-person runbook review.

Best,
Jessica Lang
Director, Infrastructure Security
Aurelia Systems

Attachment: aurelia-siem-requirements.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Date: 2026-11-01T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Observability onboarding for on-prem Redwood instance

Marissa / Diego / Mina — forwarding Aurelia's ask. Key asks: syslog vs HEC, network flows, evidence artifacts and staging checklist. Aurelia runs Splunk + Tempo. I attached their requirements from Jessica.

Quick priorities I'd like us to cover in the runbook:
- Preferred connector: our recommended pattern for private deploys is HA forwarder (HEC) with TLS mutual auth to a customer-managed ingest endpoint, OR an on-prem forwarder shim that writes signed batched manifests to an S3-compatible bucket they control (for air-gapped workflows).
- Tracing hooks: minimal header propagation we require (traceparent) and a brief for instrumenting the Redwood sidecar so traces surface in Tempo.
- Evidence: signed delivery receipts, file-level SHA256, and an audit manifest per day.
- Ports & egress: list exact ports and CIDRs for on-call/network to approve.

Can Diego draft the technical appendix (network + cert flow + ports) and Mina draft the evidence & acceptance checklist? Marissa, can you own scheduling the runbook review with Jessica next week (timebox 60m)?

Thanks — KYR.

--
Kimberly Park
Sr. Program Manager, Observability (Private Deploy)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability onboarding for on-prem Redwood instance

Kimberly / team — drafting technical appendix below (high level + example configs). I'll attach this to the runbook draft.

1) Connector recommendation (preferred -> fallback):
   - Primary: HEC push into customer-managed Splunk HEC cluster with mTLS (Redwood sidecar -> HEC endpoint). Advantages: near-real-time, structured JSON events, token rotation kept by customer.
   - Fallback: Syslog over TLS to a local forwarder (heavy forwarder / rsyslog shippers) for legacy customers. Use batching to limit rate spikes.
   - Air-gapped: Signed manifest uploads to S3-compatible endpoint, coupled with periodic delivery receipts.

2) Ports & egress (customer must open):
   - HEC: TCP 443 outbound to <customer-hec-host>:443 (mutual TLS).
   - Tracing: TCP 9411/OTLP/443 depending on customer Tempo front (we prefer OTLP/HTTP over 4318 if available).
   - Certs: Redwood requires a CA bundle from customer for mTLS; we support RSA and ECDSA certs.

3) Tracing hooks & header propagation:
   - Redwood runtime will propagate W3C traceparent and tracestate headers. Ensure customer proxies do not strip these.
   - Example: include trace.parent in logs for joinability (we add trace_id in log JSON).

4) Evidence / audit artifacts:
   - Per-day manifest: list of exported files with SHA256, timestamp, Redwood sig (ed25519).
   - Delivery receipts: HEC send receipts logged in our control plane (or signed manifest for S3 flow).
   - Retention: default 90 days in staging; production retention per contract.

5) Acceptance checklist (for staging):
   - [ ] HEC endpoint reachable and mTLS validated with test certs
   - [ ] A representative traffic replay accepted by Splunk (sample tokens present)
   - [ ] Traces show end-to-end correlation (Redwood request -> generated spans visible in Tempo)
   - [ ] Manifest & delivery receipts are generated and verifiable

Attachments planned: runbook-draft.md, example-otlp-config.yaml.

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Infra Engineer, Runtime Networking
Redwood Inference
